title: Eddie Johnson, Punch Miller and Lee Collins in Chicago
summary: Other New Orleans musicians in Chicago, and a band contest against Lee Collins's band.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: What about Eddie Johnson? Did you know him?
Yeah. He made trips with me, a couple of trips with me to Chicago, and out to the Stacks.
Which one is he? Which Eddie Johnson?
The one with Wicked Weir lines? Big head.
Big head.
Big head, that's it. You know everything.
Yeah, but I know there's more than one Eddie Johnson.
Well yeah, they had the little Eddie, the bright one, he used to play saxophone too, some
time back. Were there any other New Orleans guys up there other than Louie?
Well I saw Punch when I was up there, Punch Miller. Yeah.
In fact I didn't get around.
Did you know Lee Collins down here? Oh yeah. I know Lee used to play out there at the La Vida before I did. Lee played there a long time. Yeah I know Lee a long, long time ago.
Down here, huh? Yeah. Did you ever know him in Chicago? Ever seen him out there?
Well no, I didn't ever meet him in Chicago. I knew him from here. Yeah, I did meet him in Chicago.
I think that back.
There were two executions that went to Chicago.
I was on the I.C. and he was on the LNN, and that's the time when we had that Buckingham Contest on 47th Street, 47th Avenue.
I know the Regals, it's right around the corner, Michigan Avenue I think it is, right on the corner. We tied up there for hours. That's right.
Who did Lee have with him?

Have a pretty good band? Oh yeah, yeah, good one. Yeah, George Washington on trombone, Pedro Poenelle on alto, David Jones on tenor-sikes, Daniel Parker on guitar, he had Albert Morgan on bass, and I think it was Roy on the drums though. I don't remember the drum player, but he had a good band. Regular New Orleans? Yeah, and he had the Joe Robichaud.
Regular New Orleans band though up there, huh?
Yeah, we had the, just like we used to do it here on the streets, we did it over there.
